attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication on CentOS Stream 10 across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (read-only standbys). node1 was initialized fresh, configured with wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, listen_addresses='*', a dedicated pg_hba.conf replication rule for the replicator role scoped to node2/node3 IPs, and firewalld opened on 5432/tcp. A replicator role was created and node2/node3 were provisioned via pg_basebackup -R (streaming, writing standby.signal + primary_conninfo automatically). Verified standbys are read-only (INSERT rejected) and see primary writes. Then ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (standbys first, primary last), capturing boot_id before/after each reboot to prove real restarts, confirming postgresql service and replication/recovery state recovered after each, and finally validating a fresh write on the primary replicated to both standbys post-restart.
